summary: Resource is the loop's physical-budget governor: ResourceManager coordinates GPU, memory, and disk, computing ResourcePressure (None..Critical) from ResourceUsage. AdaptiveQuotas shrink concurrency, context tokens, and queued tasks as pressure rises; ResourceLimitTracker hands out RAII guards (GPUAllocationGuard, RequestGuard, TaskGuard) that enforce ResourceQuotas; MemoryManager emits MemoryActions (ReduceContext, OffloadModels, EmergencyRestart) under pressure; DiskManager governs checkpoints/logs/models storage and produces StorageEstimates. It is the substrate that decides how big and how parallel each loop iteration is allowed to be.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/resource/ (mod.rs, quotas.rs, memory.rs, disk.rs, gpu.rs) read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where adaptive quotas throttle the loop's context and concurrency as physical pressure rises.

examples.title: Gate a request against current quotas
examples.intent: Refuse a resource request that would exceed the loop's current limits.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AdaptiveQuotas.check compares a ResourceRequest against current quotas and returns QuotaExceeded, so the control stage blocks an act step before it over-allocates GPU or memory.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the quota gate node checks the pending request against current limits.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate glows green when the request fits, flashes red 'QuotaExceeded' when it doesn't.

examples.mini_scenario: A request for 20GB GPU is checked against a 16GB per-model quota and rejected before the model loads.
examples.pitfall: check reads current (adaptive) quotas, not base; a request that passed earlier can fail after pressure shrinks the limits.

examples.title: Shrink quotas as pressure rises
examples.intent: Automatically reduce concurrency and context as the system gets loaded.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: adjust_for_pressure maps ResourcePressure to reduced max_concurrent_requests/max_context_tokens/max_queued_tasks, so the loop iterates smaller and less parallel under load.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the pressure dial previews how quotas shrink at each pressure level.
touch_interaction.visual: Quota bars contract as the dial climbs; at Critical they snap to emergency minimums.

examples.mini_scenario: Pressure hits Medium, halving concurrency and context; the loop keeps running but with smaller, serial steps.
examples.pitfall: Pressure returning to None resets to base; a loop caching the shrunken quota misses the recovery and stays throttled.

examples.title: Enter Critical emergency mode
examples.intent: Survive Critical pressure without crashing the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: At Critical, adjust_for_pressure clamps to 1 concurrent request, 8192 context tokens, 10 queued tasks, and halves per-model GPU memory, forcing the loop into a minimal survival footprint.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the pressure badge at Critical shows the emergency clamp values.
touch_interaction.visual: The node pulses deep red; quota bars collapse to their emergency floors with a warning glow.

examples.mini_scenario: Under Critical pressure the loop drops to single-threaded 8k-context steps to avoid OOM.
examples.pitfall: 8192 is a hard floor at Critical; a task needing more context simply cannot run until pressure eases.

examples.title: Reserve GPU memory with an RAII guard
examples.intent: Hold GPU memory for the duration of a model call and auto-release it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ResourceLimitTracker.allocate_gpu_memory returns a GPUAllocationGuard that reserves bytes and frees them on drop, so the loop's GPU budget can't leak across iterations.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a model node onto the GPU lane reserves its memory as a scoped guard.
touch_interaction.visual: A GPU bar fills by the reserved amount; the fill drains when the node's scope ends.

examples.mini_scenario: A model call allocates 12GB via a guard; when the call's scope ends the guard drops and frees it automatically.
examples.pitfall: The guard frees on drop; holding it in a long-lived struct beyond the call keeps GPU memory reserved and starves the loop.

examples.title: Limit concurrent requests with a RequestGuard
examples.intent: Cap how many LLM requests run at once.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: start_request returns a RequestGuard when under max_concurrent_requests, so the loop's fanout is bounded and excess parallel work is refused, not queued unbounded.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading a fanout node reveals how many request slots are free vs held.
touch_interaction.visual: Filled slots glow; attempts beyond the cap bounce back with a red flash.

examples.mini_scenario: With a cap of 3, a fourth concurrent request fails to acquire a RequestGuard and waits its turn.
examples.pitfall: The guard releases on drop; forgetting to hold it for the request's whole lifetime under-counts real concurrency.

examples.title: Bound the task queue with a TaskGuard
examples.intent: Stop the loop from queuing unlimited pending tasks.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: queue_task returns a TaskGuard only under max_queued_tasks, so the loop applies backpressure at the queue instead of accumulating work it can't run.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a task into a full queue bounces it back.
touch_interaction.visual: The queue depth bar fills; at capacity new tasks rebound with a soft red pulse.

examples.mini_scenario: The queue hits its cap; the next submission can't acquire a TaskGuard and the caller must retry later.
examples.pitfall: Queue cap shrinks under pressure; a submitter that ignores the guard failure loses tasks silently.

examples.title: Compute pressure from usage
examples.intent: Turn raw CPU/GPU/memory/disk usage into a single pressure level.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ResourceManager derives ResourcePressure from ResourceUsage, giving control one None..Critical signal to drive all its throttling decisions.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the usage overlay collapses per-resource gauges into one pressure badge.
touch_interaction.visual: A composite badge shades green->amber->red as the worst resource climbs.

examples.mini_scenario: GPU at 92% and memory at 88% resolve to High pressure, which then shrinks the loop's quotas.
examples.pitfall: Pressure is a rollup; a single saturated resource can dominate, so inspect ResourceUsage to know which one to relieve.

examples.title: React to shared pressure across components
examples.intent: Let all subsystems see the same live pressure value.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: shared_pressure exposes an Arc<RwLock<ResourcePressure>>, so any loop stage can read the current pressure and self-throttle without polling the manager.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing an edge from the pressure bus to any node subscribes it to live pressure.
touch_interaction.visual: A shared pressure halo tints every subscribed node the same color as the bus.

examples.mini_scenario: Memory and act stages both read shared_pressure=High and each independently reduces its footprint.
examples.pitfall: It's a shared lock, not per-subscriber; holding the write lock too long stalls every reader mid-loop.

examples.title: Reduce context under memory pressure
examples.intent: Cut the context window instead of OOM-ing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MemoryManager emits MemoryAction::ReduceContext{target_tokens}, so under pressure the loop's reason stage runs with a smaller prompt rather than crashing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the context dial down issues a ReduceContext action.
touch_interaction.visual: The context bar contracts to the target; the reason node briefly flashes amber.

examples.mini_scenario: Memory hits 90%; a ReduceContext{16384} action trims the next prompt to fit available RAM.
examples.pitfall: Reducing context can drop crucial history; pair it with summarization so the loop doesn't lose task state.

examples.title: Offload models to CPU under pressure
examples.intent: Free GPU memory by moving models to CPU.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MemoryAction::OffloadModels frees GPU pressure so the loop can keep running (slower) instead of failing to allocate.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a model node from the GPU lane to the CPU lane triggers offload.
touch_interaction.visual: The model node slides across lanes; the GPU bar drops and a 'CPU' tag appears.

examples.mini_scenario: Under GPU pressure a secondary model offloads to CPU, freeing 8GB so the primary model keeps serving.
examples.pitfall: CPU offload trades memory for latency; offloading the hot-path model can tank the loop's throughput.

examples.title: Pause non-critical tasks by priority
examples.intent: Keep critical work running by pausing low-priority tasks.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MemoryAction::PauseTasks{priority_threshold} sheds work below a priority, so the loop protects its critical path when resources are scarce.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the task lane sets the pause priority threshold.
touch_interaction.visual: Tasks below the threshold dim and pause; critical tasks stay lit.

examples.mini_scenario: Under pressure, background indexing (priority 2) pauses while the user's task (priority 8) keeps running.
examples.pitfall: Set the threshold carefully; too high a threshold pauses work the user is actually waiting on.

examples.title: Trigger an emergency component restart
examples.intent: Recover a wedged subsystem when nothing else relieves pressure.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MemoryAction::EmergencyRestart is the terminal escalation, resetting a component so the loop can continue rather than deadlock at Critical.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the emergency node downward issues a restart.
touch_interaction.visual: The target component node blinks red then re-initializes with a spin-up animation.

examples.mini_scenario: A leaking component holds Critical pressure; an EmergencyRestart frees its memory and the loop resumes.
examples.pitfall: Restart loses in-flight state; only escalate here after cheaper MemoryActions have failed to relieve pressure.

examples.title: Estimate memory for a token budget
examples.intent: Know how much RAM a planned context will need.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MemoryManager.estimate_for_tokens(tokens, bytes_per_token) predicts allocation, so the reason stage can size its context to fit before committing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the context planner shows projected memory for the chosen token budget.
touch_interaction.visual: A projected-memory bar overlays the available-memory bar; overflow shades red.

examples.mini_scenario: estimate_for_tokens(32768, 100) projects ~3.3MB per the model's per-token cost, confirming the plan fits.
examples.pitfall: bytes_per_token is a coarse estimate; real KV-cache growth can exceed it, so leave headroom below the limit.

examples.title: Track allocated memory explicitly
examples.intent: Keep a running total of memory the loop has claimed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MemoryManager.allocate/free/get_allocated maintain an atomic counter, giving the observe stage an accurate view of the loop's own memory footprint.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the memory node shows current allocated bytes.
touch_interaction.visual: An allocated-memory gauge rises on allocate and falls on free.

examples.mini_scenario: get_allocated reports 2.1GB claimed by the loop, distinct from OS-level usage, guiding the next allocation.
examples.pitfall: allocate/free must be balanced; a missed free leaks the counter and makes the loop refuse future allocations.

examples.title: Reserve a multi-resource budget for a step
examples.intent: Claim GPU, memory, and disk together for one heavy operation.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A ResourceRequest (gpu/system_memory/disk bytes + duration) becomes a ResourceReservation, so the act stage holds a coherent budget for a step and releases it on completion.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a heavy-op node onto the reservation lane claims a bundled budget.
touch_interaction.visual: Three sub-bars (GPU/mem/disk) fill together; releasing drains all three at once.

examples.mini_scenario: A fine-tune step reserves 12GB GPU + 4GB RAM + 20GB disk for ~10 min, then releases on finish.
examples.pitfall: release() must be called (or the reservation dropped); a leaked reservation blocks the resources for the whole run.

examples.title: Report disk usage and headroom
examples.intent: Know how much storage is left before the loop writes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DiskManager surfaces DiskUsage (used/total/available/percent), so the observe stage can warn control before checkpoints or model downloads exhaust disk.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the disk node zooms from a percent badge to a used/available breakdown.
touch_interaction.visual: A disk gauge fills; above a threshold it shades amber then red.

examples.mini_scenario: DiskUsage shows 94% used; the loop defers a large model download until space is reclaimed.
examples.pitfall: percent hides absolute headroom; 6% free on a 4TB disk is fine, on a 20GB disk it isn't, so read available bytes.

examples.title: Estimate storage needs ahead of time
examples.intent: Plan disk usage for a run before committing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DiskManager.estimate_storage_needs(days) yields a StorageEstimate (checkpoints/logs/models/buffer), so the reason stage can plan retention within available disk.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the storage-estimate node breaks total into checkpoints/logs/models/buffer.
touch_interaction.visual: A stacked bar shows each category's projected size summing to the total.

examples.mini_scenario: estimate_storage_needs(7) projects 18GB total; the loop confirms the 40GB free disk can hold a week of runs.
examples.pitfall: total() sums the categories including buffer; ignoring the buffer term underestimates true headroom needs.

examples.title: Create state dirs lazily on first write
examples.intent: Avoid polluting the user's cwd with empty state directories.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DiskManager defers checkpoints/logs/models dir creation until an actual write (ensure_dir), so read-only loop commands don't scatter empty directories.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a state-dir node shows whether it exists yet or is deferred.
touch_interaction.visual: Deferred dirs render as dashed placeholders; they solidify on first write.

examples.mini_scenario: `selfware config show` builds a DiskManager but creates no dirs; the first checkpoint write makes checkpoints/.
examples.pitfall: Because creation is deferred, code that assumes the dir exists before any write will hit a missing-path error.

examples.title: Select a quantization level to fit GPU
examples.intent: Trade precision for a smaller GPU footprint.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: GpuManager's QuantizationLevel lets the reason stage pick a lower-precision model variant so it fits the available GpuDevice memory, keeping the loop runnable on constrained hardware.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the quantization dial cycles precision levels and shows the resulting GPU footprint.
touch_interaction.visual: As precision drops, the projected GPU bar shrinks; the chosen level is highlighted.

examples.mini_scenario: The model won't fit at full precision, so the loop selects a lower QuantizationLevel that fits the 16GB GpuDevice.
examples.pitfall: Lower quantization degrades output quality; over-quantizing to fit can make the reason stage unreliable.

examples.title: Escalate MemoryActions in order under rising pressure
examples.intent: Relieve pressure with the cheapest effective action first.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The MemoryManager's action handler applies MemoryActions in increasing severity (RunGC/FlushCaches -> ReduceContext -> PauseTasks -> OffloadModels -> EmergencyRestart), so the loop degrades gracefully instead of jumping straight to a restart.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking up the escalation ladder steps through successively stronger actions.
touch_interaction.visual: A ladder of action rungs lights bottom-up; each rung glows as it fires, red at the top.

examples.mini_scenario: Pressure rises: first FlushCaches, then ReduceContext, then PauseTasks each buy relief before any restart is needed.
examples.pitfall: Skipping straight to OffloadModels/EmergencyRestart wastes the cheaper actions and disrupts the loop unnecessarily.
